title: SoundGraph Board Profile
description: Describes one physical board: which processor target it uses and how audio and controls are wired. A board profile is data consumed by the generic firmware — it must never alter graph semantics. Target (esp32-s3) and board (this file) are deliberately separate: the target defines architecture and memory constraints, the board defines pins and peripherals.

id.description: Stable identifier, used to select the profile at build time.

target.description: Processor target the generic firmware is built for.

kind.description: i2s-dac: an external or onboard DAC driven over plain I2S with no control channel (PCM5102 and friends). codec: a chip that also needs I2C configuration.

mclk.description: -1 or absent when the DAC needs no master clock.

amp.description: The speaker power amplifier's enable line, when it has one. Smart-speaker boards often route it through an I2C I/O expander rather than a chip GPIO.

gpio.description: Direct chip GPIO, when it is one.

pin.description: Expander pin number, e.g. 8 for EXIO08.

audio_in.description: Shape mirrors audio_out. Absent means the board has no audio input; AudioInput nodes then produce silence, exactly as in a browser without getUserMedia.

controls.description: Physical performance controls, for later mapping onto patch control surfaces.
